intro: Lithophane turns a photo into a 3D part that shows the image against the light: dark areas are thicker and let less light through, and light ones are thin and glow. It is a classic 3D printing gift, as a plate, curved to stand up or as a cylinder for a lamp.

Choose the shape, the width in millimetres (for the cylinder, the perimeter) and the minimum and maximum thicknesses: 0.8 and 3 mm work well with white PLA. The resolution sets how many pixels per millimetre are used; with 5, each pixel is 0.2 mm, more than a 0.4 nozzle can tell apart.

The result is a closed solid with a flat or smooth back face (on curved ones, the inside), ready to print. Print it upright or with the relief facing up, at 100% infill and in white so light passes through well. If you will view it from the other side, tick mirror.

Use photos with good contrast and large faces; very small details get lost. Each photo is processed in an isolated process on our server in the European Union, up to five per task, and deleted when it expires.
steps: Choose the shape, width and thicknesses.
Download the STL and print it in white.

Because you are viewing it from the other side. Generate it again with mirror ticked.

faq.q: How long does it take to print?
faq.a: It depends on the size: a 100 mm plate usually takes 2 to 4 hours.
